title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is smooth projective of dimension n, φ: Y ↪ X is a smooth hyperplane section of dimension n−1, and L_X is cup product with the hyperplane class. The notes work at the level of 'Poincaré–Hodge algebras', i.e. abstract cohomology with Lefschetz operator, primitive decomposition H*(X)=⊕_{i+2j≤...} L_X^j P^i(X), and correspondences acting on it. (The neighbouring pages are unrelated documents, a Karoubi note and a Hartshorne-type text on injective sheaves, so they give no context.)

Step 1, decomposition (*). By weak Lefschetz, φ^* is injective on H^{≤n−1}(X). Restriction sends primitive classes to primitive classes, and φ^* commutes with L. Hence φ^* kills the top Lefschetz pieces L^{n−i}P^i(X) and is injective on the others. This gives H*(Y) = (⊕_{i+j≤n−1, i,j≥0} L_X^j P^i(X)) ⊕ E^{n−1}. The first summand is identified with its image φ^*(...). E^{n−1} is the vanishing (primitive, orthogonal) part of H^{n−1}(Y).

Step 2. Since φ_*φ^* = L_X, the Gysin map φ_* acts on the first summand as L_X: it sends φ^*(L^jP^i) to L^{j+1}P^i. This is injective because j+1 ≤ n−i. The map φ_* vanishes on E^{n−1}.

Step 3, corollary:
- Ker φ_* = E^{n−1}(Y).
- Im φ_* = Im L_X = ∩_{0≤i≤n} Ker p_i^X, where p_i^X is the projector onto the primitive piece P^i(X).
- H*(Y) = Im φ^* + E^{n−1}.
The grade-shift relations are p_i^X φ_* = 0 and p_j^X φ_* = φ_* p_{j−2}^Y. Here φ_* raises degree by 2, so the second relation is naturally read with Künneth/degree projectors.

Step 4, the basic identities:
- φ^* L_X = L_Y φ^*.
- L_X φ_* = φ_* L_Y (projection formula).
- φ_*φ^* = L_X.
- φ^*φ_* = L_Y (self-intersection formula, since the normal bundle is O(1)|_Y).
A crossed-out attempt proves the last one by checking both sides on E^{n−1} and on Im φ^*.

Purpose: an algebraic (correspondence-theoretic) formalism of the Lefschetz/hyperplane-section relationship. It serves the inductive approach to the standard conjectures (Lefschetz-type B(X) and Hodge-type) via hyperplane sections.
errors: Notation p_i is overloaded. In 'Im L_X = ∩ Ker p_i^X' the p_i are primitive-part projectors, while in 'p_j^X φ_* = φ_* p_{j−2}^Y' they behave like degree (Künneth) projectors. With degree projectors, 'p_i^X φ_* = 0 for 0≤i≤n' would be false: it holds only for i=0,1.

The identification of φ_* with L_X tacitly identifies L_X^jP^i(X) with its image under φ^*. That φ^* is injective there and that the sum with E^{n−1} is direct uses hard Lefschetz on X: if x∈H^{n−1}(X) and Lx=0 then x=0. This is not stated on the page.
Minor: the page writes H*(Y) = Im φ^* + E^{n−1} immediately after discussing Im φ_*. The justification 'Im φ_* = Im φ_*φ^*' is correct only because φ_* kills E^{n−1}.

ideas.what: Decomposition of the cohomology of a smooth hyperplane section into the restricted Lefschetz pieces of X plus the vanishing part E^{n−1}
ideas.modern_name: Weak + hard Lefschetz; vanishing cycles decomposition H^{n−1}(Y)=φ^*H^{n−1}(X) ⊕ Ker φ_*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lefschetz; algebraic setting Deligne (Weil I/II), SGA 7 XVIII (Deligne–Katz)
ideas.where_published: Standard-conjecture literature: Grothendieck 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969), Kleiman 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (1968)

ideas.what: Ker φ_* = E^{n−1}, Im φ_* = Im L_X, and the identities φ_*φ^*=L_X, φ^*φ_*=L_Y, projection formula
ideas.where_published: Kleiman 1968 uses these for the inductive proof that B(X) reduces to middle degree

ideas.what: Expressing the hyperplane-section relationship purely by correspondences/projectors (p_i, L, φ_*, φ^*) in an abstract 'Poincaré–Hodge algebra'
ideas.modern_name: Abstract Lefschetz modules / motivic Lefschetz decomposition
ideas.where_published: Only partially, in the 1969 standard conjectures paper

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine Lefschetz bookkeeping for a hyperplane section in an abstract correspondence formalism. All of it is standard and appears in Kleiman's 1968 exposition and later literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Corollaire Ker φ_* = ... Ker E^{n−1}(Y)': after the crossed-out material, the intended statement is Ker φ_* = E^{n−1}(Y). The 'Ker' before E is the start of a struck-out attempt or is spurious.
'Im φ_* = Im φ_*φ^* = I[?]' is most likely 'Im φ_* = Im φ_*φ^* = Im L_X' or similar.
'enfin on φ_*φ^* = L_X' should read 'et φ_*φ^* = L_X'.
The marginal boxed word reads roughly '[-...-] variantes' (crossed out), unclear.
